title: 2Method
use_cases: Use when constructing training examples to improve large-scale models' long-context utilization.
Implement when training on datasets that lack explicit meta-information or structural hierarchies.
Configure when simulating long continuous documents by setting the breadth hyper-parameter k to 1.
Use when wanting to increase dependency density within training batches compared to random example packing.
Implement when training retrieval-augmented language models to establish stronger text segment dependencies.
content:
SPLiCeis a method of constructing the training examples that allows improvement of large-scale models’ long-context utilization and, consequently, their performance on a range of tasks. Through experimental study, we positively validate that such an approach leads to better long-context capabilities.
##### Rationale and intuitions
Capturing long-range dependencies is believed to enhance language modeling, e.g. as demonstrated in the study by> (Borgeaud et al., [> 2022
](#bib.bib5)> )
which highlights the advantages of incorporating global dependencies in retrieval-augmented language models. However, in typical datasets, the occurrence of such dependencies is rare> (de Vries, [> 2023
](#bib.bib10)> )
and diminishes as the distance between elements increases, leading to challenges in model learning. Our approach addresses this challenge by focusing on increasing dependency density, achieved by creating training examples that consist of multiple related documents. The rationale of this strategy is reinforced by the work of> Levine et al. (
[> 2022
](#bib.bib19)> )
, which shows that the trained model establishes stronger dependencies between text segments present in the same training example.
In our work, we study the following methods:
##### Baseline
The standard approach, commonly used in LLM training pipelines> (Brown et al., [> 2020
](#bib.bib6)> )
, is to randomly sample documents from the dataset and concatenate them to make training examples of a desired context (also known as example packing).
##### Repository-level code data
Certain datasets encompass meta-information regarding the data structure, which can be utilized to devise training examples. Take, for instance, a dataset consisting of GitHub repositories (e.g.,> (Li et al., [> 2023b
](#bib.bib22)> )
): rather than grouping documents randomly into a single context, we might group documents based on their subdirectory in a repository, thereby crafting a training example with potentially more cross-document dependencies compared to those generated randomly. This methodology, elaborated in> (Wu et al., [> 2022
](#bib.bib37)> )
, led to notable perplexity enhancements with augmented context length, suggesting that data orchestrated in such a manner could exhibit valuable long-context training signals. In our study, we strive to quantify the advantages of this methodology against the random packing baseline outlined above while maintaining the set of training documents to eliminate potential confounders.
![Refer to caption](extracted/5326715/Figures/diagram_tree2.png)Figure 2:Visualization ofSPLiCetraining example generation.
##### Structured Packing for Long Context (SPLiCe)
The additional structure provided by meta-information is unavailable in most datasets. We propose to overcome this challenge by using a retrieval method to identify related documents. We test two choices of retrieval methods BM25> (Robertson & Zaragoza, [> 2009
](#bib.bib28)> ; Bassani, [> 2023
](#bib.bib4)> )
and Contriever-MSMARCO> (Izacard et al., [> 2022
](#bib.bib16)> )
). With those tools at our disposal, we proposeSPLiCe, a method that creates training examples by building a tree of documents. It starts from a randomly sampled document and continues in a breadth-first manner, expanding each node with top-k𝑘kitalic\_ksimilar documents from the corpus. The final sequence consists of a flattened tree according to a certain traversal strategy (e.g., level-order traversal). An intuitive visualization ofSPLiCeis presented in Figures[1](#S1.F1)and[2](#S2.F2), while a detailed pseudocode is given in Algorithm[1](#alg1). We note that the general formulation ofSPLiCeis flexible. For example, the parameterk𝑘kitalic\_kallows for interpolation between two modes of retrieval. Fork=1𝑘1k=1italic\_k = 1SPLiCecreates a path of related examples simulating a long document. For larger values ofk𝑘kitalic\_kour method generates examples that are similar to the ones used by retrieval augmented models. Note that the dataset must be reasonably curated forSPLiCeto work efficiently. For example, a low duplication rate incentivizes the model to utilize long context beyond simple copying.
